label: 05 Direct MQTT trigger
info: Nuclio consumes MQTT messages directly; Node-RED publishes test messages and observes the output topic.

label: 06 Cron trigger
info: Nuclio owns the schedule and invokes the function at the configured interval. Refresh the function Run logs to observe each tick.

label: 07 Direct NATS trigger
info: Nuclio subscribes directly to NATS for request/reply, and Node-RED publishes and observes a second function through NATS's built-in MQTT bridge.

name: demo-mqtt-transform
configCode:
apiVersion: "nuclio.io/v1"
kind: NuclioFunction
spec:
  build:
    commands:
      - pip install paho-mqtt
  triggers:
    mqtt:
      kind: mqtt
      url: mosquitto:1883
      attributes:
        subscriptions:
          - topic: demo/mqtt/input
            qos: 0

configCode:

kind: NuclioFunction

name: Same request, six runtimes
info: Compare the same simple invocation across Python, Go, Node.js, Shell, Java, and .NET Core. Java and .NET Core are lazy so their tech-preview runtimes do not block the core gallery; send the explicit deploy command before invoking them.

name: Lazy deployment and input commands
info: This function does not deploy at startup. Send deploy before the first normal invocation; status, redeploy, and rebuild are explicit input commands.

name: Batch four messages
info: The function trigger batches four incoming messages. The burst generator makes the batching behavior easy to reproduce without a repeating inject.

name: Create four-message burst
func:
const values = [1, 2, 3, 4];
return [values.map(value => ({ payload: { value }, topic: "batch-demo" }))];

name: Retries, fallback, environment, and scaling
info: The first function returns a deliberate HTTP 503 when fail=true, so the invoke node retries twice before its fallback output. The second demonstrates a runtime environment variable and a two-replica configuration.

name: Direct MQTT trigger
info: Node-RED publishes a test message to Mosquitto. Nuclio subscribes directly, transforms it, and publishes the result to a second topic. The message does not pass through the Nuclio HTTP invoke node. MQTT triggers are currently a Nuclio tech-preview feature.

name: Nuclio-owned schedule
info: Nuclio owns this 30-second interval; Node-RED only declares and observes the function. Open the function Status tab and refresh Run logs to see each invocation. This demonstrates a schedule, not durable batch orchestration or backfill support.

name: NATS request/reply
info: Nuclio consumes demo.nats.input directly and returns the handler result on the NATS request reply subject. Run: docker run --rm --network node-red-contrib-nuclio_default natsio/nats-box:latest nats request -s nats://nats:4222 demo.nats.input '{"message":"hello"}'. NATS triggers are currently a Nuclio tech-preview feature.

name: Node-RED input/output through NATS MQTT
info: Node-RED publishes to NATS's MQTT listener on demo/nats/mqtt/input. The Nuclio NATS trigger handles the message and publishes the transformed result natively to NATS on demo.nats.mqtt.output; NATS's MQTT bridge delivers it to Node-RED on demo/nats/mqtt/output. NATS MQTT requires JetStream and is enabled by the local compose fixture.
